rows.note: A server that lists no tools has a digest: the empty array.
A tool with only a name: description is "" and inputSchema {} in the contract digest.
Two ordinary tools.
The same two tools listed in the other order.
The same tools with other whitespace and member order in the text.
No description.
description null counts as no description; description is a contract member whatever it holds, so it is in neither digest.
A description that is not a string counts as none in the contract digest.
An empty description is the same contract as none.
No inputSchema.
inputSchema {} is the same contract as none.
An inputSchema that is not an object counts as none in the contract digest.
No outputSchema.
outputSchema {} is a different contract from no outputSchema.
An outputSchema with content.
outputSchema null counts as absent in the contract digest.
A tool with the four contract members only.
The same tool with title, annotations, icons, _meta and a vendor member: the same contract digest, and now an extras digest.
destructiveHint true becomes false: the contract digest does not move, the extras digest does.
An argument limited to an enum.
The same tool with the enum gone and the description unchanged: the contract digest moves.
The same tool with one more sentence in its description.

rows.note: Code-unit order puts Z_tool before a_tool; a locale collation would not.
Code-unit order: resume, rezume, résumé; a locale collation gives resume, résumé, rezume.
A shorter name sorts before a longer one it begins.
U+1F600 (surrogates D83D DE00) sorts before U+E000 by UTF-16 code unit; by code point it would sort after.
The same two names written as the characters themselves.
Two tools share a name: both are kept, ordered by their canonical bytes.
The same two listed in the other order.
The same tool listed twice stays twice.
Arrays keep their order: required [a, b].
required [b, a] is another contract.
Member names are sorted by UTF-16 code unit, also when they are not ASCII.
Every way JSON lets the same doubles be written.
The same doubles in the form RFC 8785 writes them.
9007199254740993 has no double of its own: it is digested as 9007199254740992.
9007199254740992, which the previous vector rounds to.
1e400 has no IEEE 754 double.
Neither has -1e400.
A number with no double outside the contract members: the contract digest stands, the extras digest cannot be computed.
An array nested 509 deep under inputSchema.x reaches level 512: the deepest a reader accepts.
One level more under inputSchema.x reaches 513: the contract digest cannot be computed.
An array nested 510 deep in a member outside the contract reaches level 512.
One level more in that member: the extras digest cannot be computed, the contract digest stands.
A description that is an array nested 600 deep is not a string, so it counts as none and reaches neither digest: no TSD-DEPTH.
description 1e400 is not a string, so it counts as none and reaches neither digest: no TSD-NUMBER.
1e400 in a member outside the contract: the contract digest stands, the extras digest cannot be computed.
Every escape JSON has, and characters JSON.stringify leaves alone (U+007F, U+2028, U+2029).

rows.note: \u0041 and A are the same string.
The same description written as the characters themselves.
é as one code point (U+00E9).
é as e and a combining accent (U+0065 U+0301): another string, another digest. Nothing is normalised.
A high surrogate with no low one after it.
A low surrogate with no high one before it.
A low surrogate followed by a high one.
A lone surrogate in a tool's name.
A lone surrogate in a member name.
A lone surrogate outside the contract members: the contract digest stands, the extras digest cannot be computed.
The extras of extras-present under another description: another contract digest, the same extras digest.
Only the tools that carry extras are in the extras object.

rows.note: A tool declares readOnlyHint true.
Only readOnlyHint changes to false: the contract digest stays equal and the extras digest changes.
Numbers in extras, in forms JSON allows.
The same doubles in the form RFC 8785 writes them.
Tool names are member names of the extras object, so they are sorted by UTF-16 code unit: U+1F600 before U+E000.
A description that is not a string and an inputSchema that is not an object are contract members by name: in neither digest.
Two tools share a name and one of them carries extras: the extras object holds that one.
The same two in the other order.
Two tools share a name and both carry extras: an object keyed by name cannot hold both.
Two tools share a name, both carry extras, and the first listed holds a lone surrogate in them: TSD-NAME and TSD-TEXT both apply, and section 10 reports TSD-NAME.
The same with a number that has no double in the first one's extras: TSD-NAME and TSD-NUMBER both apply, and section 10 reports TSD-NAME.
A member name repeated in a tool object: the last value is the one read (section 3.4). Equal to the same tool with only the last description.
The tool of repeated-member-description written with only its last description.
name repeated, the first empty and the last valid: the last is read, so the tool is valid.
name repeated, the first valid and the last empty: the last is read, so the entry has no name and TSD-TOOL applies to both digests.
A member name repeated inside inputSchema: the last value is read at every depth.
The tool of repeated-member-in-schema written with only the last type.
A member outside the contract repeated: the contract digest is that of the tool without it, and the extras digest uses the last value.
The tool of repeated-member-extras written with only the last title.
The same member name written once plainly and once with an escape is one name after parsing: the last value is read.
The tool of repeated-member-escaped-name written with only the last description.
description repeated, a string first and a number last: the last is read, it is not a string, so the description counts as none.
A tool named a with nothing else: what repeated-member-name-last-valid and repeated-member-type-change read.
An entry that is not an object.
An entry that is null.
An entry that is an array.
A tool with no name.
A tool whose name is the empty string.
A tool whose name is a number.
One entry that is not a tool: the whole set has no digest.
A lone surrogate in the first tool and an entry with an empty name after it: TSD-TOOL and TSD-TEXT both apply, and section 10 reports TSD-TOOL for both digests.
